descriptionChirho: Piel: to deceive, beguile, or deal treacherously with someone; always used of interpersonal deception or betrayal. Consistently glossed across languages as 'deceive' (Arabic khadaa, Hindi dhokha diya, Korean soginda, Spanish enganar). Occurs in narratives of personal betrayal: Gen 29:25 (Laban deceived Jacob), 1 Sam 19:17 and 28:12 (deception of Saul/by Saul), Josh 9:22 (Gibeonites' deception), 1 Chr 12:18 (potential betrayal), Prov 26:19 (one who deceives his neighbor), Lam 1:19 (allies deceived me).

Qal participle feminine: to be high, raised, or lifted up; likely belonging semantically to root I ramah 'be high' rather than root II 'deceive,' but catalogued here. In Num 15:30 describing sin committed 'with a high hand' (yad ramah), i.e., defiantly. Glosses: Arabic murtafi'a 'elevated,' Hindi uunche uthe hue 'raised up high,' Korean nop-eun 'high,' Spanish alzada 'raised.'
